children: The India Leadership Conversation, titled ‘From Scale to Significance: Building Hospitality Businesses That Last’, brought together leaders from across hotel companies and leisure businesses to examine what makes a hospitality enterprise sustainable over the long term

The 10th edition of the prestigious BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026), hosted at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity, is bringing leading voices from across the hospitality industry for the next two days of conversations on the sector’s growth and evolution. With the theme
‘India’s Hospitality Decade: From Growth to Greatness’
, the Summit will examine the opportunities, challenges and shifts shaping India’s hospitality landscape as the industry enters a defining decade.
As India’s hospitality market continues to expand, the conversation around growth is increasingly moving beyond room additions and geographic scale. The
India Leadership Conversation
, titled
‘From Scale to Significance: Building Hospitality Businesses That Last’
, brought together leaders from across hotel companies and leisure businesses to examine what makes a hospitality enterprise sustainable over the long term.
The discussion was chaired by
Ajay K Bakaya, Chairman, Sarovar Hotels and Director, Louvre Hotels India
, and brought together

Jatin Khanna, CEO, Sarovar Hotels; Rahool Macarius, Market MD Eurasia, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts; Vikram Lalvani, MD & CEO, Sterling Holiday Resorts; Neelendra Singh, MD & CEO, Lemon Tree Hotels; and Samir MC, CEO, Tamara Leisure Experiences

Khanna said, “It is important for brands to take a look at the scale of serving customers. Scale isn’t just about numbers. I believe that AI will take over the world, but our job is definitely safe. Technology will be on the commercial side, but people will remain at the centre of our business.”

Macarius, quoted, “Our brand is the largest franchise in India. When we entered the country, we became aspirational in these cities. To succeed in India, we built a national sales team and focussed on creating value for owners in half the time. The result is that owners who started by building one hotel with us are now developing four or five hotels with us.”

Lalvani, addressed, “Scale thrills, but significant compounds. The destinations are the actual content. Today, our basic DNA is to unveil a new destination. We have our own legacy, and today, we get to our destination because we understand why the traveller wants to get to a specific destination.”

Singh, explained, “On one side, we have an engine that needs to produce talent, while on the other is the sourcing engine, which sometimes remains fundamentally weak. We may have to look beyond hospitality schools to build the talent pool we need.”

Samir MC said, “Our focus is on making the guest journey experiential, as guests remember us because of the small things we do, not because of what they see in the room. We are very tech-enabled, which helps us create a strong guest preference system that allows us to remember every guest from one property to another.”

The session wrapped up with a clear message: true growth in Indian hospitality is about endurance rather than raw numbers. The panel agreed that building lasting industry leadership requires moving beyond aggressive hotel openings to focus on operational resilience, consistent guest satisfaction, and rock-solid owner relationships that withstand market cycles.

The two-day BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) encompasses over 25 sessions where hospitality veterans and experts across the nation gathered to provide diverse knowledge and insights. The Summit & Awards is a testament to BW Hotelier’s commitment towards revolutionising Indian hospitality by honouring the crème de la crème of the industry.
